summary: Describes a mechanism for forwarding multicast based only on IGMP or MLD group membership information. In simple topologies, a device need not run a multicast routing protocol; it can learn membership and proxy it upstream. It is a standards-track document.

eli5.summary: A small router in the middle can just pass on who wants what, like an assistant relaying requests.

questions: how does igmp proxy forwarding work
subtitle: How a simple edge device can forward multicast using only IGMP or MLD group membership, with no multicast routing protocol.

tldr.problem: In a simple tree of devices, such as an edge box with one link to the core and many to customers, running a full multicast routing protocol adds cost and operational work.
tldr.mechanism: The device acts as an IGMP/MLD router on its downstream interfaces and as an IGMP/MLD host on its single upstream interface. It merges downstream memberships into one database, reports that upstream, and forwards packets according to it.
tldr.outcome: It only works in a manually configured tree within one administrative domain, and a non-proxy device winning the Querier election or an upstream loop breaks it.

today: RFC 4605 is a Proposed Standard published in August 2006. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why Proxy Instead of Route
sections.content:
In a simple tree topology it is not necessary to run a multicast routing protocol. It is enough to learn group membership, proxy it, and forward multicast packets based on it. The RFC's typical example is an edge aggregation box such as a Digital Subscriber Line Access Multiplexer (DSLAM), which usually has one connection to the core network and many to customers.

Skipping protocols such as PIM or DVMRP reduces both the cost of the device and the operational overhead. It also makes the proxy independent of whichever multicast routing protocol the core routers use, so it can be deployed in any multicast network. A hot spare connection to the core can serve as the upstream connection, and the proxy upstream connection can be updated when the edge box fails over to it.
sections.eli5: If your street has only one road out, you do not need a big map. The box just remembers who wants what and passes it along.

sections.title: Where It Applies
sections.content:
IGMP/MLD-based forwarding only works in a simple tree topology. The tree must be configured by hand by designating upstream and downstream interfaces on each proxy device. There are no multicast routers other than proxy devices inside the tree, the root is expected to connect to a wider multicast infrastructure, and the protocol is limited to a single administrative domain.

If the topology is not a tree, a more robust failover mechanism is wanted, or more than one administrative domain is involved, a multicast routing protocol should be used instead.
sections.eli5: This trick only works for a neat tree shape in one neighbourhood. For a tangled web of roads, you need proper maps.

sections.title: The Proxy Design
sections.content:
A proxy device has a single upstream interface (toward the root, also called the Host interface) and one or more downstream interfaces (also called Router interfaces). These are explicitly configured; no protocol determines them. The device performs the router portion of IGMP or MLD on downstream interfaces and the host portion on the upstream interface. It MUST NOT perform the router portion on the upstream interface.

It sends membership reports upstream when queried, and sends unsolicited reports or leaves when its database changes. For forwarding, it builds a list of the upstream interface plus every downstream interface that has a matching subscription and on which it is the IGMP/MLD Querier. It removes the interface the packet arrived on and forwards to the rest.

Senders inside the tree work because all traffic is forwarded toward the root. The routers at the root should be configured to treat systems inside the proxy tree as if directly connected. This is likely manual configuration, since the proxy gives upstream routers no way to learn which networks are behind it.
sections.eli5: The box asks the kids below what they want, like a teacher, and asks the grown-ups above for it, like a kid. Then it passes the right things down to the right kids.

sections.title: The Membership Database
sections.content:
On each downstream interface the proxy runs the router side of IGMP/MLD, with the version explicitly configured and defaulting to the highest the system supports. The result is a set of subscriptions per interface, which are merged into a membership database of records (multicast-address, filter-mode, source-list).

Before merging, IGMPv1 and IGMPv2/MLDv1 subscriptions are converted to IGMPv3/MLDv2 form and timers are removed. If the filter mode is EXCLUDE, every source whose source timer is above 0 is removed. The merge then uses the rules for multiple memberships on one interface from RFC 3376 and the MLDv2 specification. For example, an IGMPv2 subscription (G) on one interface and an IGMPv3 subscription (G, INCLUDE, (S1, S2)) on another merge to (G, EXCLUDE, NULL).

Upstream, the proxy uses IGMPv1 or IGMPv2/MLDv1 if such a querier is on the upstream network, and otherwise IGMPv3/MLDv2. With IGMPv3/MLDv2, database changes are reported as if the proxy were a host. With the older versions only creation or deletion of records is reported, and only the multicast address is used.
sections.eli5: The box keeps one big list of every channel anyone below wants, merging duplicates, and tells the grown-ups above only what is on that combined list.

sections.title: Forwarding and the Querier Rule
sections.content:
A proxy forwards packets from its upstream interface to each downstream interface according to that interface's subscriptions and whether the proxy is the Querier there. Packets from a downstream interface go to the upstream interface and to every other downstream interface under the same conditions. A forwarding cache MAY be used, but it MUST be updated whenever its inputs change.

Requiring the forwarder to be the Querier "piggy-backs" forwarder election on Querier election, which gives similar functionality on the local link to the PIM Assert mechanism and avoids local loops and redundant traffic. Because the lowest IP address wins the election, proxies must be given the lowest addresses on the link, or a non-proxy Querier will stop traffic flowing. With only one proxy on a link, the rule MAY be disabled, but the default configuration MUST include it.

For Source-Specific Multicast, the proxy should follow the IGMPv3 for SSM specification (RFC 4604) for both its host and router roles. IGMPv1 or IGMPv2 subscriptions to SSM addresses should be ignored, and packets with source-specific addresses SHOULD NOT be forwarded to interfaces with such subscriptions.
sections.eli5: Only one helper per street is allowed to hand out the channels, chosen by who has the lowest house number, so nobody gets two copies.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Since only the Querier forwards, a non-forwarder elected Querier creates a black hole. An attacker on a downstream LAN can get itself elected Querier so that no packets are forwarded. The RFC says operators SHOULD assign the subnet's lowest IP address(es) to the proxy or proxies.

There is no upstream loop detection, so it MUST be administratively assured that such loops do not exist. Also, because the proxy presents the aggregate of all downstream membership, access control applied at the upstream router cannot be applied to a single subscriber; it applies equally to all interested hosts behind the proxy.
sections.eli5: A bully could pretend to be the helper and then hand out nothing. Giving the real helper the lowest number stops that.

viz.caption: THE TWO ROLES OF A PROXY DEVICE

items.title: Upstream interface
items.text: Acts as an IGMP/MLD host. Sends reports when queried and unsolicited reports or leaves on change.

items.title: Downstream interfaces
items.text: Act as IGMP/MLD routers. Their subscriptions are merged into the membership database.

items.title: Forwarding rule
items.text: Forward to upstream plus downstream interfaces with a matching subscription where the proxy is the Querier.

layers.label: Upstream interface
layers.detail: Host portion of IGMP/MLD reports the merged state

layers.label: Downstream subscriptions
layers.detail: Per-interface state from the router portion of IGMP/MLD
